punchline: Sinclair says the DNA text stays intact; what wears out is the layer that decides which genes get read.
thirty_sec: David Sinclair calls aging one disease with one root: cells keep their DNA but lose epigenetic information, the methyl marks that decide which genes are read. He says doctors chase one illness at a time and gain lifespan but not healthy years. Mouse work after his book restored vision in old mice, but that is mice, and critics say the theory remains untested.
